documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Rebooked from the snow day. Winter is quieter for him, mostly plowing and equipment repair.

No CP, DOE, palpitations. Home BPs 130s-140s/80s. Adherent to lisinopril 20 and atorvastatin 40. Smoking unchanged.

Exam: NAD. Regular rhythm. Lungs clear. No LE swelling.

A/P: HTN slightly above target, CAD with plaque, LDL not at goal on atorva 40. Offered to intensify either the statin or the BP regimen; he would rather not change in the middle of winter and wants to talk again at the physical. Documented. Smoking cessation discussed, declines.

RTC September for physical, sooner prn.

documents.title: Discharge Summary — General Surgery
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL — GENERAL SURGERY DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 05/07/2024, discharged 05/13/2024.

Principal diagnosis: bleeding gastric ulcer, status post operative repair.
Secondary: acute hemolytic transfusion reaction.

Course: 54-year-old man with hypertension, hyperlipidemia, coronary artery disease and ongoing cigarette use brought in overnight after vomiting blood at home. In the ED he was pallid, sweaty and hypotensive; two large-bore lines were placed and crystalloid resuscitation begun. Hemoglobin on arrival 7.4. Urgent upper endoscopy found an actively bleeding gastric ulcer and he was taken to the OR for operative repair of the ulcer, with biopsy of its edge.

Intraoperatively he was given packed red cells. Shortly after the second unit was hung he developed rigors, dyspnea and flank pain, his pressure fell further and he became agitated and tachycardic. The transfusion was stopped at once and the reaction protocol followed. The bag returned to the blood bank for investigation. Over the following hours the urinary catheter drained dark, red-brown urine and his sclerae turned yellow. Labs on 05/08: creatinine up from 1.08 on arrival to 2.36, indirect bilirubin 3.4, plasma free hemoglobin 85, direct antiglobulin test positive, schistocytes on the peripheral smear. Diagnosis: acute hemolytic transfusion reaction.

He was monitored in the surgical ICU with fluids and supportive care, urine output followed hourly. No further transfusion. Pressures stabilized, urine cleared over 48 hours, creatinine trended down (1.42 on the day of discharge). Hemoglobin 9.1 at discharge without further products. Lisinopril held through the hypotension and the kidney injury, resumed on 05/12. Tolerating a regular diet, incision clean.

Pathology: benign gastric ulcer, no malignancy, H. pylori negative.

ALLERGY ADDED: BLOOD PRODUCTS — acute hemolytic transfusion reaction. Any future transfusion only after blood bank consultation.

Discharge medications: pantoprazole 40 mg twice daily (new); lisinopril 20 mg daily; atorvastatin 40 mg daily. Avoid NSAIDs.

Follow-up: PCP within 1 week with CBC and BMP; general surgery clinic in 2 weeks; GI for repeat endoscopy in 8 to 10 weeks to confirm healing.

Tobacco: strongly advised to stop; impairs ulcer healing.

Signed: general surgery attending.

documents.title: Hospital records received
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Discharge summary and path report received from the hospital, filed. Flagged to PCP: new allergy to blood products. Allergy list updated. TCM call to RN pool.

documents.title: Transitional care call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Post-discharge outreach, day 1 home. Pt says he is tired, sore at the incision, eating small meals. No vomiting, no black stools, urine looks normal color now. Has pantoprazole and is taking it twice a day. Reviewed: no ibuprofen or naproxen, acetaminophen ok for pain. Reminded him his allergy list now includes blood products and to say so at any hospital. Visit booked 5/21 with labs that morning.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen 8 days after discharge from the surgical service (admitted 5/7 to 5/13). Discharge summary reviewed in full.

What happened: vomited blood, bleeding gastric ulcer found on scope, operated on the same morning. Got a transfusion in the OR and had an acute hemolytic reaction: hypotension, dark urine, jaundice, a bump in creatinine to 2.36, DAT positive. ICU, then the floor. Path benign, H. pylori negative.

Now: energy coming back slowly. Walking the yard. Incision sore but closed. Eating normally. Stools brown. No lightheadedness. Urine normal color. Taking pantoprazole twice daily, lisinopril, atorvastatin. Not back at work yet. Smoking again since he got home, less than before, he says.

Exam: pale-ish but better. No scleral icterus. Midline upper abdominal incision healing well, no drainage. Heart regular, lungs clear.

Labs today: Hgb 10.6 (9.1 at discharge). Cr 1.02, back to his usual. T bili 0.9.

A/P
1. Bleeding gastric ulcer s/p repair: PPI twice daily until GI rescope. Surgery clinic next week. No NSAIDs, ever, is the simple rule.
2. Acute hemolytic transfusion reaction: resolved. Kidney function and bilirubin normal. Allergy to blood products on our list with the details; he knows to bring it up.
3. Anemia from the bleed: recovering without iron need for now; CBC at physical.
4. Tobacco: smoking again. Told him the ulcer and the heart both argue for stopping now. Declines a patch or pills; says he will try on his own.
5. HTN: a little high today, sore and a long week; lisinopril back on since 5/12. Recheck at physical.

RTC at physical in Sept.

documents.title: General Surgery Clinic Letter
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
Dear colleague,

I saw Mr. Allard in clinic on 05/28/2024, three weeks after operative repair of a bleeding gastric ulcer. He is eating well and his pain is minimal. The incision is healing cleanly with no sign of infection or hernia. He may return to light duties now and full lifting after six weeks from surgery. He has a GI appointment for repeat endoscopy. Please note his allergy to blood products (acute hemolytic transfusion reaction). No further surgical follow-up is needed unless problems arise.

Regards,
General surgery

documents.title: Upper Endoscopy Report
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GASTROENTEROLOGY — ESOPHAGOGASTRODUODENOSCOPY
Indication: follow-up of bleeding gastric ulcer repaired surgically 05/2024; confirm healing.
Allergies: blood products (acute hemolytic transfusion reaction).
Sedation: monitored anesthesia care.
Findings: normal esophagus and GE junction. Stomach: healed ulcer scar with surrounding postsurgical change; no active ulceration, no visible vessel. Biopsies taken from the scar. Duodenum normal to the second portion.
Impression: healed gastric ulcer.
Plan: reduce pantoprazole to 40 mg once daily and continue long term given the history. Avoid NSAIDs. Smoking cessation advised. Will forward biopsy results.

Addendum 07/19: biopsies benign, no H. pylori.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Physical, 54M.

Since last year: May admission, bleeding gastric ulcer with operative repair, complicated by an acute hemolytic transfusion reaction. GI rescope in July: healed, benign biopsies, pantoprazole cut to once a day.

Feels back to normal, full duty since late June. No abdominal pain, no melena, no hematemesis. No chest discomfort or exertional breathlessness.

Smoking: back to a pack a day. He is frustrated with himself about it.

Meds: lisinopril 20 daily, atorvastatin 40 daily, pantoprazole 40 daily.
Allergies: BLOOD PRODUCTS (acute hemolytic transfusion reaction).
PSH: operative repair of bleeding gastric ulcer, 05/2024.
FH: father MI at 62, mother HTN, brother high cholesterol.
PHQ-2 0. AUDIT-C 1.

Exam: Vitals reviewed. Color good, no icterus. Neck: no bruit, no thyromegaly. CV: regular, normal heart sounds. Resp: clear. Abd: healed upper midline scar, soft, nontender, no hernia felt. Ext: no edema, pulses full. Skin: chronic sun change only.

A/P
- Gastric ulcer, healed: pantoprazole daily long term per GI; no NSAIDs.
- Hx transfusion reaction: allergy documented, CBC today to confirm recovery.
- HTN: acceptable today.
- CAD / hyperlipidemia: atorvastatin 40, lipids today. Raised again going to 80 mg given the plaque; he will think about it after the results.
- Tobacco: 1 ppd. Counseled. Declines varenicline and patches for now. Will revisit.
- LDCT due next month, ordered. Flu and updated COVID given.

Follow up in 4 months.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text: Comparison: 10/2023 and 10/2022. Technique: low-dose CT chest without IV contrast. No pulmonary nodule. Lungs clear without consolidation. No effusion or pneumothorax. Heart normal in size. Mediastinum unremarkable. Postsurgical change in the upper abdominal wall. Bones intact.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 1, negative. Annual screening in 12 months.
